report.summary: Chunk 4 of mapping/reach.py: helper functions for branch literal extraction, dispatch chain detection, dead branch and import error analysis, and import splitting with context awareness.
risks: _branch_literals | medium | Only handles str constants in comparisons, BoolOp, and startswith/endswith calls; misses other patterns like 'x == y' where y is a variable. | Add handling for ast.Name or ast.Str? Actually ast.Constant covers all constants in Python 3.8+; but variable comparisons are missed. Could add ast.Name with lookup if symbol table available, but not needed if scope is limited.

_dispatch_chains | medium | Uses ast.walk which visits every node; might double-count nested ifs but uses seen set to avoid. However, chains from different top-level ifs might share nodes if nested; seen prevents recursion but may skip valid chains. | Verify with test cases where ifs are nested inside other ifs.

_split_imports | low | Recursive descent may miss imports inside comprehensions or lambda bodies because ast.iter_child_nodes does not descend into those by default (they are expressions). However, comprehensions are rare for imports. | Confirm that ast.iter_child_nodes covers comprehension generators? Actually it does, as comprehensions have generators which are child nodes. But lambda bodies are not iterated because ast.Lambda has a body that is a single expression, not a statement list. So imports inside lambdas are missed. Acceptable.

_is_never_true | low | Only checks ast.Constant with falsy value; does not detect ast.NameConstant (deprecated) or ast.Name with known falsy constant (e.g., if False). But in Python 3.8+, bool constants are ast.Constant, so it's fine.
todos: Consider adding support for ast.Name in _branch_literals for cases like 'if x == y' where y is a variable (string constant not available).
Add handling for ast.Str and ast.Bytes for Python 3.7 compatibility if needed (currently ast.Constant covers all).
Test _dispatch_chains with nested ifs inside else branches to ensure chains are correctly detected.

handoff.purpose: Helper functions for branch literal extraction, dispatch chain detection, dead branch detection, import error catching, and import splitting with context.

symbols.name: _branch_literals
symbols.note: Extracts string literals from branch conditions (comparisons, BoolOp, startswith/endswith calls).

symbols.name: _dispatch_chains
symbols.note: Finds if/elif chains with at least _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES branches, returns list of (literal, node) pairs per chain.

symbols.name: _DEAD_BRANCH
symbols.note: String constant for dead branch reason.

symbols.name: _SUPPRESSED
symbols.note: String constant for suppressed import reason.

symbols.name: _IMPORT_ERRORS
symbols.note: Tuple of exception names considered import errors.

symbols.name: _is_never_true
symbols.note: Checks if test is a constant falsy literal (if False/0).

symbols.name: _catches_import_error
symbols.note: Checks if a try block has a handler that catches ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError.

symbols.name: _split_imports
symbols.note: Splits imports into live and weak lists based on branch context (dead branches, suppressed imports).

claims.text: A chain is only a command table when it is long enough (``_MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES``); shorter ones are ordinary conditionals and reporting them as subcommands would fabricate entry points.
claims.why: _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``if False:`` / ``if 0:`` -- a branch the interpreter deletes. Deliberately literal-only. Inferring that some NAME is falsy would make the walk guess, and a guess in this direction silently deletes real edges.
claims.why: Function checks ast.Constant with falsy value, which covers False and 0 literals.

claims.text: Does this ``try`` swallow a failing import? Narrow on purpose: only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count. A bare ``except Exception`` around an import is usually a lazy-optional-dependency idiom too, but widening this rule reclassifies real edges on evidence that is not there.
claims.why: Function checks handler type names against _IMPORT_ERRORS tuple, which includes ImportError and ModuleNotFoundError. It does not handle bare except or Exception.

claims.text: Structural descent rather than ``ast.walk`` because the whole point is the CONTEXT an import sits in: the same statement is evidence in one branch and not in another.
claims.why: Function uses recursive descent with rec() helper, passing 'why' string to track context. It handles If, Try nodes specially to adjust context.

claims.text: the else IS the live branch
claims.why: In _is_never_true if, body is dead, so orelse is the live branch; rec is called on orelse without why (i.e., why='').

claims.text: the handler's own import is the fallback that actually runs
claims.why: After marking body and orelse as suppressed, handler body is processed with why unchanged (which may be empty or suppressed).

observations.what: _branch_literals only extracts string literals from comparisons where left is a constant string; it does not handle cases like 'x == "foo"' where x is a variable.

_dispatch_chains uses ast.walk which visits all nodes; the seen set prevents infinite loops but may miss chains that are nested inside other ifs because once a node is seen, it is skipped even if it could be part of another chain.

_split_imports uses ast.iter_child_nodes which does not descend into function/lambda bodies (except comprehensions? Actually it does descend into comprehension generators). Imports inside lambdas or nested function definitions are missed.

_catches_import_error checks for ast.Attribute with attr in _IMPORT_ERRORS; this catches cases like 'import errors.ImportError' but not 'import errors as err; except err.ImportError'. However, typical usage is just 'except ImportError'.
